questions.question_english: What is the constitutional implication of placing 'Education' in the Concurrent List (Entry 25) for a school Principal in Delhi?
options_english: The Principal must strictly follow Central statutory rules while completely ignoring local state laws like the Delhi School Education Act.

questions.explanation_english: Education's placement on the Concurrent List (Entry 25) subjects school administration in Delhi to both Central statutes (like RTE Act) and state legislation (like Delhi School Education Act). Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
Assertion (A): No citizen shall be denied admission into any educational institution maintained by the State or receiving aid out of State funds on grounds only of religion, race, caste, or language.
Reason (R): This protection is expressly guaranteed under Article 29(2) of the Constitution of India.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: Article 29(2) explicitly provides that no citizen shall be denied admission into any educational institution maintained by the State or receiving aid out of State funds on grounds only of religion, race, caste, language or any of them. The assertion reflects the text of Article 29(2), and the reason correctly cites the governing provision.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर A है। अनुच्छेद 29(2) राज्य द्वारा संचालित या राज्य निधि से सहायता प्राप्त किसी शैक्षणिक संस्थान में प्रवेश के समय धर्म, मूलवंश, जाति या भाषा के आधार पर भेदभाव से नागरिकों की रक्षा करता है। कारण इस संवैधानिक संरक्षण का सही संदर्भ बताता है। इसका उद्देश्य यह सुनिश्चित करना है कि सार्वजनिक या सहायता-प्राप्त शिक्षा संस्थानों में प्रवेश निर्णय केवल इन निर्दिष्ट आधारों पर भेदभावपूर्ण न हों।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 29(2) explicitly provides that no citizen shall be denied admission into any educational institution maintained by the State or receiving aid out of State funds on grounds only of religion, race, caste, language or any of them. The assertion reflects the text of Article 29(2), and the reason correctly cites the governing provision.

questions.subject: UPSC Principal Paper
questions.question_english: Read the situation below and answer the question that follows: A recognized private unaided school in Delhi claims minority status based on religion to avoid implementing the 25% EWS/DG quota mandated by the RTE Act. What is the constitutionally correct position regarding this claim?
options_english: Unaided minority schools must fulfill the 25% quota as they operate on land allotted by the government.
Only aided minority schools are exempt from the RTE mandate.
All private schools, without exception, must implement the 25% quota under Article 21A.
Unaided minority schools are exempt from the RTE mandate of 25% EWS reservation.
questions.explanation_english: In Pramati Educational and Cultural Trust (2014), the Supreme Court held that the RTE Act, including its mandatory 25% EWS quota, does not apply to minority educational institutions (both aided and unaided) covered under Article 30(1), as enforcing it would infringe upon constitutional rights granted to minorities.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर D है। प्रमती एजुकेशनल एंड कल्चरल ट्रस्ट (2014) निर्णय के अनुसार RTE अधिनियम का 25% EWS कोटा अनुच्छेद 30(1) के अंतर्गत संरक्षित अल्पसंख्यक शैक्षणिक संस्थानों पर लागू नहीं होता। इसलिए यदि विद्यालय विधिसम्मत रूप से अल्पसंख्यक संस्थान है, तो केवल RTE अधिनियम के इस कोटे के आधार पर उसे गैर-अल्पसंख्यक निजी विद्यालय जैसा दायित्व नहीं दिया जा सकता। यह निष्कर्ष संस्थान के वास्तविक अल्पसंख्यक दर्जे और लागू कानूनी स्थिति पर निर्भर करेगा।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Unaided minority schools are exempt from the RTE mandate of 25% EWS reservation.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: In Pramati Educational and Cultural Trust (2014), the Supreme Court held that the RTE Act, including its mandatory 25% EWS quota, does not apply to minority educational institutions (both aided and unaided) covered under Article 30(1), as enforcing it would infringe upon constitutional rights granted to minorities.

questions.subject: UPSC Principal Paper
questions.question_english:
Examine the following statements about the Seventh Schedule and Educational Administration:
I. Before 1976, the Central Government had very limited legislative authority over school education.
II. The transfer of education to the Concurrent List enabled the creation of overarching national frameworks like the RTE Act.
III. The State Governments have lost all legislative powers over education after the 42nd Amendment. 
Which of the above statements are correct?
options_english: I and II
I and III
II and III
I, II and III
questions.explanation_english: Before 1976, school education was in the State List, restricting Central legislation. Shifting education to the Concurrent List enabled central laws like the RTE Act. Statement III is incorrect because State Governments retain broad legislative and administrative powers over education concurrently with Parliament.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: I और II। 42वें संविधान संशोधन से पहले शिक्षा राज्य सूची में थी, इसलिए केंद्र की सामान्य विधायी भूमिका सीमित थी। 1976 में शिक्षा समवर्ती सूची में आई, जिसके बाद संसद और राज्य विधानमंडल दोनों शिक्षा से संबंधित कानून बना सकते हैं। तीसरा कथन गलत है: राज्यों ने अपनी सारी शक्ति नहीं खोई; वे शिक्षा पर विधायी और प्रशासनिक भूमिका बनाए रखते हैं, जबकि केंद्रीय कानून से टकराव होने पर अनुच्छेद 254 लागू हो सकता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I and II

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Before 1976, school education was in the State List, restricting Central legislation. Shifting education to the Concurrent List enabled central laws like the RTE Act. Statement III is incorrect because State Governments retain broad legislative and administrative powers over education concurrently with Parliament.

questions.question_english: Which Constitutional Amendment shifted the responsibility of "Education" from the State List (List II) to the Concurrent List (List III)?
options_english: 24th Amendment Act
42nd Amendment Act
44th Amendment Act
86th Amendment Act
questions.explanation_english: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 transferred 'Education' from the State List (List II, Entry 11) to the Concurrent List (List III, Entry 25). This landmark legislative shift empowered Parliament to frame national education policies and statutes alongside State Legislatures, unifying educational standards across India.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर 42वाँ संशोधन अधिनियम है। 1976 के 42वें संशोधन ने शिक्षा को राज्य सूची की प्रविष्टि 11 से हटाकर समवर्ती सूची की प्रविष्टि 25 में रखा। इसके बाद संसद और राज्य विधानमंडल, दोनों को शिक्षा के कई पहलुओं पर कानून बनाने की शक्ति मिली। इससे शिक्षा से संबंधित संघ-राज्य समन्वय का संवैधानिक ढाँचा बदला, जबकि कानूनों में टकराव की स्थिति अनुच्छेद 254 के अधीन आती है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) 42nd Amendment Act

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 transferred 'Education' from the State List (List II, Entry 11) to the Concurrent List (List III, Entry 25). This landmark legislative shift empowered Parliament to frame national education policies and statutes alongside State Legislatures, unifying educational standards across India.

questions.question_english:
Examine the following statements about the role of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) and the Right to Education:
I. NCPCR is a constitutional body established under Article 338B.
II. NCPCR is mandated to monitor the child's right to education under the RTE Act, 2009.
III. NCPCR can inquire into complaints regarding the violation of the right to free and compulsory education. 
Which of the above statements are correct?
options_english: I and II
II and III
I and III
I, II and III
questions.explanation_english: NCPCR is a statutory body established under the Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005 (not a constitutional body under Article 338B), making statement I incorrect. Statements II and III accurately describe NCPCR's statutory mandate under the RTE Act, 2009 to monitor child rights and inquire into violations.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: II और III। NCPCR एक वैधानिक निकाय है, जिसे बाल अधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम, 2005 के अंतर्गत स्थापित किया गया; यह अनुच्छेद 338ख के अंतर्गत संवैधानिक निकाय नहीं है। RTE अधिनियम के अंतर्गत इसे बच्चों के शिक्षा-अधिकार की निगरानी और उल्लंघन संबंधी शिकायतों की जाँच की भूमिकाएँ दी गई हैं। इसलिए पहला कथन गलत है, जबकि दूसरे और तीसरे कथन सही हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) II and III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: NCPCR is a statutory body established under the Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005 (not a constitutional body under Article 338B), making statement I incorrect. Statements II and III accurately describe NCPCR's statutory mandate under the RTE Act, 2009 to monitor child rights and inquire into violations.

questions.question_english: Read the situation below and answer the question that follows: The Directorate of Education issues a circular requiring all schools, including unaided private schools, to sing the National Anthem. A minority institution objects, stating it violates their religious freedom under Article 25. Which precedent established by the Supreme Court governs this scenario?
options_english: Bijoe Emmanuel v. State of Kerala
St. Stephen's College v. University of Delhi
TMA Pai Foundation v. State of Karnataka
In Re Kerala Education Bill
questions.explanation_english: In Bijoe Emmanuel v. State of Kerala (1986), the Supreme Court held that Jehovah's Witness students who stood respectfully without singing the National Anthem during assembly were protected under Article 19(1)(a) and Article 25, as forcing them to sing violated their genuine religious convictions.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर बिजो इमैनुएल बनाम केरल राज्य है। 1986 के इस मामले में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने माना कि यहोवा के साक्षी समुदाय के विद्यार्थी राष्ट्रगान के समय सम्मानपूर्वक खड़े रह सकते हैं, लेकिन अपने धार्मिक विश्वास के कारण उसे गाने से इंकार करने पर उन्हें दंडित नहीं किया जा सकता। निर्णय ने राष्ट्रीय प्रतीकों के सम्मान और अंतरात्मा/धर्म की स्वतंत्रता के बीच संतुलन पर विचार किया।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Bijoe Emmanuel v. State of Kerala

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: In Bijoe Emmanuel v. State of Kerala (1986), the Supreme Court held that Jehovah's Witness students who stood respectfully without singing the National Anthem during assembly were protected under Article 19(1)(a) and Article 25, as forcing them to sing violated their genuine religious convictions.

key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Entry 25

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Entry 25 of the Concurrent List (List III) in the Seventh Schedule covers education, including technical education, medical education, and universities. This entry is explicitly subject to Entries 63, 64, 65, and 66 of List I, which reserve coordination, higher education standards, and national importance institutions for exclusive Parliamentary legislation, ensuring overall national standard alignment.
